summary: The audit checks 10 units from one emphasis list (Cultural & Social, Environmental or Medical) and 20 more units of ANTHRO courses, with at most 5 units of directed reading or research, toward the 30 units the minor needs. Every course needs a C or better; at least 15 units must be ANTHRO courses numbered 100 or above, at most 5 units may be S/NC, and at least 20 units must be ANTHRO, since at most 10 may come from related areas, overseas study or transfer. Approved department courses off an emphasis list, a self-designed emphasis and petitioned outside units are moved in by hand. You check by hand the C average, the two essential ANTHRO courses, and your faculty advisor and declaration.

totals.why: Transfer: "No more than 10 units may be approved from related areas of study, overseas studies, and transfer units." With the 30-unit total, that is at least 20 units in ANTHRO.

yA8BptcM.why: "Students should complete a minimum of 10 units from the courses listed below." The emphases are "Fulfill ANY of the following requirements", and Grading says "At least 10 units must be taken from the chosen ANTHRO emphasis": one emphasis, 10 units from its list. "Departmental courses outside of this list may be counted toward emphasis but will need faculty advisor approval", so those are moved in by hand, and a self-designed emphasis is an exception from the undergraduate committee.

Bx11AqQY.why: "The remainder of the 30 required units may be fulfilled with any Anthropology courses, or a combination of Anthropology courses and up to successfully petitioned 10 units from related areas of study": 30 less the 10 emphasis units is 20. "No more than 5 units of directed reading-style/ research coursework listed may be counted toward the minor." The minor lists no research courses; the cap uses the department's research list from the major (ANTHRO 92A/B, 93, 94, 95, 95B, 96, 97, 199).
